main_text.p: biles, & ab omni concretione li-beras,& alias secundas & mutabi-les, quod ex materia constent & forma, aperte exprimit Aristote-les primo sapientiæ libro,nec à ratione alienum est, quoniam rerum aliæ æternæ sunt & divinæ, aliæ caducæ ortui interituique obnoxiæ. Præterea τῶν ὄντων [?] quædam non reipsa,sed duntaxat ratione à materia seiunguntur, in quibus mathematica scientia consistit. Mathematicus enim cuncta quæ sub sensum cadunt, cuiusmodi est gravitas, levitas, durities, mollities, frigus,calor,humor,ariditas, atque aliæ huius generis sensiles affectiones mente ex corpore abstrahit, atque separat, ac id duntaxat, quod quantum est nudum relinquit, ac meditatur, quemadmo-

page.notes: The line "aliæ" in the sentence "quoniam rerum aliæ æternæ" carries a printed mark, and "primo" is partly obscured by a crease. The Greek "τῶν ὄντων" is only partly legible; the article may be read differently. The signature "** 2" at the foot is doubtful. Show-through text from the reverse page appears faintly at the bottom and is left out.
